statement: What is the smallest positive integer $n$ for which $n! = 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 \cdots n$ is divisible by $2^{10} = 1024$?

choices.misconception: I found the smallest n with n! at least 1024, which is 7 since 7! = 5040, but being bigger than 1024 is not the same as being divisible by it.
I matched the exponent and guessed n = 10 because of 2^10, but 10! has only 8 factors of 2.
I counted only two factors of 2 in 8 instead of three, so I thought 12! had just 9 factors of 2 and went on to 14.
I counted one factor of 2 for each even number, so I thought I needed ten even numbers, all the way up to 20.

hints: Count the factors of $2$ in $n!$ by going through the even numbers one at a time.
The even numbers $2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12$ contribute $1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2$ factors of $2$.
Keep a running total and stop as soon as it reaches $10$. Odd numbers add nothing.

solutions.reliable: Only even factors contribute $2$s. Keeping a running total: $2$ gives $1$; $4 = 2^2$ brings it to $3$; $6$ to $4$; $8 = 2^3$ to $7$; $10$ to $8$; $12 = 2^2 \cdot 3$ to $10$. So $11!$ has only $8$ factors of $2$, while $12!$ has exactly $10$. The smallest $n$ is $12$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
